newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy committed to help Albania help itself - Dini.
newsitem.headline: Italy committed to help Albania help itself - Dini.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini, opening a conference on Albania, said the international community would help the Balkan state rebuild but Albanians had to assume responsibility for consolidating democracy.

"All of us, and certainly Italy, are committed to helping Albania with a vast range of programmes, provided that Albania takes upon itself the primary responsibility for its own future," Dini said in a speech opening the conference.
The donors' conference, called to discuss how to rebuild Albania's shattered economy, was held in the presence of new Albanian Prime Minister Fatos Nano, who triumphed in a recent general election.

The day-long meeting, attended by delegations from 35 countries and international organisations, will be followed by a larger conference on the future of Albania due to be held in Italy in the autumn.

"A certain degree of conditionality will be applied to Albania, certainly not as a way of penalizing the country and its people but as an instrument to encourage the correct implementation of agreed measures...," Dini said.
Speaking in English, Dini said a "package approach" was needed to restore normality to Albania after months of unrest.

The collapse of shaky investment pyramid schemes earlier this year swallowed the life savings of tens of thousands of Albanians and triggered months of anarchy which led to the fall of the right-wing government of former President Sali Berisha.
"Democratization, stabilisation, security and economic development go hand in hand," Dini said.
Italy has borne the brunt of the Albanian crisis. More than 14,000 refugees flooded into Italy across the southern Adriatic earlier this year aboard a flotilla of rusty ships.
In a bid to restore order and secure safe elections, Rome led a 7,000-strong multinational security force to Albania. The force is due to complete its withdrawal on August 12.
Dini told the conference that while major multilateral and bilateral donors would help Albania create sustainable economic growth, the reforms had to be more far-reaching.
"Economic growth alone will not bring about stability and progress," Dini said.
"One lesson that we have all learned from the recent events is the importance of a corresponding strengthening of the country's administration and of its democratic institutions."
Now that a new Albanian government was in place, Dini said, the expectations of the international communtiy were high.

"The international community expects a major effort...from all the Albanian parties," he told delegates. "Law and order must be restored in Albania and respect of human rights and democratic standards enhanced," he added.

The Albanian premier said on Wednesday he hoped Thursday's conference would not only produce financial backing, but also a commitment to help in development programmes in Albania, which has Europe's poorest economy.
